Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dil . ov. h OILG OPINION NO. 83 20 25 JUL 08 2025 MA. ANA ADDELLIA C. ELABA Secretary to the Sanggunian Municipality of Balangiga Province of Eastern Samar Dear Sanggunian Secretary Elaba: This pertains to the Resolution adopted by the Municipality Balangiga requesting this Department's opinion on whether the period of 'three days' mentioned in Section 5(d) of P.D. 449 (Cockfighting Law of 1974) for the conduct of cockfights during local fiestas also applies to Sundays and legal holidays. Per representation, BAGAMO Inc., a licensed cockpit operator in the Municipality of Balangiga, Eastern Samar, conducted a cockfight under the belief of its General Manager that Section 5(d)1 of Presidential Decree No. 449 authorizes the holding of cockfights for a period of three (3) days not only during local fiestas but also on Sundays and legal holidays. Specifically, the General Manager interpreted the provision to permit cockfights commencing two (2) days prior to, or alternatively, extending up to two (2) days after, a Sunday or a legal holiday, treating the said holiday or Sunday as the central day within the three-day period. Said interpretation, however, stands in contrast with the position of the Sangguniang Bayan, which maintains that the three-day maximum allowance for cockfighting under Section 5(d) applies only to local fiestas, and not to Sundays or legal holidays. Hence, the request for clarification. First off, the Department needs to highlight the fitting declaration of the Supreme Court in Canet v. Decena2, where the Court stressed that "cockfighting although authorized by law is still a form of gambling" and that gambling in general is "essentially antagonistic to the aims of enhancing national productivity and self-reliance." It was further held therein that statutes which permit gambling activities should be strictly construed, and any doubt must be resolved in favor of limiting, rather than expanding, the scope of such laws. Section 5(d) Holding Of Cockfights. Except as provided in this Decree. cockfighting shall be allowed only in licensed cockpits during Sundays and legal holidays and during local fiestas may also be held during provincial. city or municipal agricultural. commercial or industrial fair, carnival or exposition for a similar period of three days upon resolution of the province, city or municipality where such fair, carnival or exposition is to be held, subject to the approval of the Chief of Constabulary or his authorized representative: Provided that. no cockfighting on the occasion Of such a fair, carnival or exposition shall be allowed with the month of a local fiesta or for more than two occasions a year in the same city or municipality x x x. 2 G.R. No. 155344, January 20, 2004. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

With this as premise. and upon review of the pertinent provision, it is the Department's opinion that the successive period of three days mentioned in the first statement of Section 5(d) of P.D. 449 applies solely to the conduct of cockfights during local fiesta and does not extend to Sundays or legal holidays. The interpretation of this provision is governed by well-settled principles of statutory construction. Foremost among these is the rule that when the words of a statute are clear, plain, and free from ambiguity, it must be given its literal meaning and applied without attempted interpretation.3 This principle, known as the 'plain meaning rule' or verba legis, rests on the presumption that legislative intent is best discerned from the words actually used in the statute. The contested portion in Section 5(d) of P.D. 449, when read in its plain and ordinary meaning, does not support the extension of the three-day period to any days outside the local fiesta. The provision is unambiguous in limiting the holding of three-day period of cockfights to local fiesta, and there is no mention of Sundays or legal holidays as exceptions. Therefore, unless a Sunday or legal holiday coincides with the fiesta, they do not fall within the three-day period specified in the law. Moreover, the principle of ad proximum antecedens fiat relatio nisi impediatur sententia, which translates to "relative words refer to the nearest antecedent, unless it be prevented by the context'4, further reinforces this interpretation. In Section 5(d), the nearest antecedent to the phrase "for not more than three days" is the term "local fiestas". Indeed, the three-day limitation pertains specifically to the duration of cockfights during such fiestas. There is no indication in the text that such duration also applies to Sundays and legal holidays as separate occasions. Further buttressing and lending greater weight to the foregoing interpretation is the mid portion of Section 5(d), which authorizes the holding of cockfights during "provincial, city or municipal agricultural, commercial or industrial fairs, carnivals or exposition for a similar three-day period", subject to a resolution by the local legislative body and the approval of the Chief of Constabulary or his authorized representative. Notably, the said clause imposes a limitation that cockfighting in such events shall not be held within the same month of the celebration of local fiesta. This restriction clearly shows the intention of the law to avoid overlapping or extending the permitted periods for cockfighting beyond what is explicitly allowed. It shows that the law intends to treat each authorized occasion whether a fiesta, a fair, a carnival, or an exposition -- as a separate and distinct event, each with its own maximum of three days for cockfighting. Ergo, it becomes evident that the three-day period mentioned in Section 5(d) is strictly limited to these enumerated special events. The law does not include Sundays or legal holidays among these authorized occasions. If it had intended to do so, it would have clearly expressed so, as it did for fiestas, fairs and similar events. So also, the seemingly omission of Sundays and legal holidays from the list of events to which cockfighting can be permitted for up to three successive days is a telling indication that such days were not meant to be included. 3 Chavez v. JBC. G.R. NO. 202242, July 17, 2012. san Juan v. peop/0, G.R. No. G.R. No. 236628. January 17. 2023. Page 2 of 3
